Notes

钱包会记恨我

记恨 means hold a grudge. The lyric gives the wallet enough personality to resent its owner, then to reject incoming financial luck. The practical fear of wasting money expands into the absurd idea that money itself might refuse to cooperate.

  • Genius community transcript
财运

财运 is specifically financial luck, rather than luck in general. The anxious shopper imagines that offending his wallet could repel future income: money management becomes an almost personal relationship with fortune.

  • Genius community lyric text
翻跟头

翻跟头 literally means turning a somersault. Here it is a sudden reversal or humiliating setback. The sequence treats being carefree, pleased, and successful as reasons to expect punishment rather than security.

  • Genius community lyric text
皇帝的新衣

The Emperor’s New Clothes is Andersen’s tale of a ruler who parades in nonexistent clothes while everyone pretends to admire them. Here a search for the right pants leads to being stripped, displayed on a float and continually embarrassed. The reference joins the shopping scene to that fantasy of public exposure.

  • The Hans Christian Andersen Centre: The Emperor’s New Clothes
一不做二不休

一不做，二不休 means that once an action is begun, one goes through with it without stopping halfway. Its paired numbers, “one” and “two,” give the declaration a compact rhythmic shape. The refrain answers the preceding hesitation with an all-or-nothing decision.

  • Genius community transcript
快刀斩乱麻

快刀斩乱麻 pictures a sharp knife slicing through tangled hemp: handle a complicated problem decisively. Together with 坐以待毙, “sit waiting for death,” the image turns shopping indecision into the urgent language of survival and ambition.

  • Genius community transcript
没做大就不能回家

The song begins with the tiny practical problem of finding acceptable pants. By this refrain, “making it big” has become a condition of returning home at all. That jump in scale makes ordinary consumer frustration part of a much larger demand to succeed.

  • Genius community lyric text
